title: Big Bill Smith's band in Lexington and the Fess Williams comparison
summary: After a short stint with Harry Stevens he joined Big Bill Smith's band in Lexington, which Dickenson compares to Fess Williams's band and prestige.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: So what was the next band you went out with after that?

I went down to... Oh, I went with another band called Harry Stevens(?). But it was a very short engagement(?). So the next group, I would say, I went down to Lexington, Kentucky, to a band called Big Bill Smith's

Band. He was a very big guy who played alto saxophone. And in the days before I got there, he had been pretty big guy, you know. He was around the same time as...oh, I'm trying to think of his name... Fess Williams. Do you know Fess Williams?

He was around the same time as Fess Williams, right there. Fess Williams was going pretty good there in New York ...(?), and he was going pretty good in there because ...(?). He had a small band, five or six pieces that ...(?).(?).
Everybody knew about Fess Williams, in and out of Kentucky... Boy, he was a real champion, you know. [INAUDIBLE MONEY]
Well, he was making a lot of money, I guess.

He made good. I don't know if he made a lot of money, but he made a very good name for himself. Probably the kind of people ...(?). make a lot of money in ...(?).(?).(?). I'm not making a lot off money. Never did. But Fess had a big name going to ...(?).(?)., you know. I wouldn't say that he made an awful lot of money.
He was at the Savoy for a long time.
He was like before the Savoy Sultans.

He had prestige, though, in his heyday. Everybody thought he was the greatest band in the world. But it didn't sell; it wasn't selling. I don't think anybody made a whole lot of money in them days. But it gave you prestige. It was a jumping-off point. You know?
